body.statement:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(M=|\Omega|\).  For the switching coverage sets and protocol weights,
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,
              \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
       \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S),
 \qquad \min\varnothing=+\infty.
\]
The full incidence relation is computable with at most \(2^m\) distinct source-oracle queries and \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) work, and \(M\le k2^L\).  Branch-mask dynamic programming or protocol-subset enumeration, whichever is smaller, returns an exact optimum and a lexicographically first canonical singleton-ownership certificate in
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})
\]
time.  A singleton owner is stored by one index using \(\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\) bits, so the ownership contribution for all branches is \(M\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\), not \(M^2\).  Weighted greedy returns an \(H_M=\sum_{r=1}^M r^{-1}\) approximation in \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) time whenever the instance is feasible.
body.proof_tex:
For clarity, all claims in this proof concern the finite operational predicate \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  They do not assert that this predicate is semantically complete on a larger model class.

We first prove the cover identity.  If \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\) is accepted, take \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\).  Every \(\alpha\in\Omega\) has one owner.  The owner supplies a successful quadruple \((S,\ell,T,\tau)\), so the definition of \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}\) gives \(\alpha\in K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\).  Hence
\[
 \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega.
\tag{1}
\]
The distinct-protocol cost definition gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})=\sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
\tag{2}
\]
Taking an infimum over accepted certificates proves that the left side of the asserted identity is at least the cover minimum.

Conversely, let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\) satisfy (1).  For every branch \(\alpha\), choose the lexicographically first \(S_\alpha\in\mathcal P\) with \(\alpha\in K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_\alpha)\), and then choose the lexicographically first witnessing \((\ell_\alpha,T_\alpha,\tau_\alpha)\).  Make one singleton-ownership record per branch.  By the definition of \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}\), every record passes all local checks, including positivity of its own event and measured ancestry.  The records partition \(\Omega\).  For every branch its successful source triple belongs to the decoded collection, so the exhaustive source loop encounters that success; hence the specified complete run does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), and all clauses of \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) hold.  Deleting a protocol in \(\mathcal P\) that owns no selected branch cannot increase cost because \(w(S)\ge0\).  Thus the constructed certificate has cost at most \(\sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S)\).  Minimizing and combining with (2) proves
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,cup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
\tag{3}
\]
The family of protocols is finite and the costs are nonnegative binary rationals, so whenever the cover family is nonempty the minimum in (3) is attained.

We next enumerate the incidence relation.  There are \(2^m\) protocol masks.  Catalogue scans check SELECT cardinality, at-most-once mechanisms, precedence, conflicts, and allowed values; the published CTF-REALIZE runtime lemma checks physical compatibility in polynomial time.  Query \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) once for each legal mask and cache the response, so at most \(2^m\) distinct queries are issued.  For each response enumerate the \(2^L\) labels.  Retain a label exactly when it is consistent and its asserted event has positive support.  This is precisely the denominator check in equation (2) of the normal-form proof; zero mass in an unused cell is irrelevant.  Each retained slice has at most \(|V|\) canonical single-district factors, and measured ancestry is a finite endpoint/fixed-value check.

For a factor branch whose free request positions have domain sizes \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\), the equality type is induced by its assignment and creates no further choice.  The literal table contains \(q_h\) distinct request literals for position \(h\).  Since \(q_h\le2^{q_h}\) for every positive integer \(q_h\),
\[
 |\Omega_j|=\prod_{h=1}^r q_h
 \le2^{\sum_{h=1}^r q_h}
 \le2^L,
 \qquad
 M=\sum_{j=1}^k|\Omega_j|\le k2^L.
\tag{4}
\]
For every surviving \((S,\ell,T,\alpha)\), construct the value-matching graph and execute the deterministic ancestor--district recursion.  Proposition \(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) decides failure on its stated connected inputs, and Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) supplies and verifies a canonical successful trace.  Thus all witnesses for \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\) are found.  Conversely, every witness in the definition is among the enumerated masks, factors, branches, and traces.  The enumeration is therefore exact.  Its number of local branch checks is at most
\[
 2^m2^L|V|M
 \le 2^{m+2L}|V|k,
\tag{5}
\]
and all oracle payload bits actually inspected are charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  Equations (4)--(5) prove the stated \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) incidence-construction bound.

List the legal protocols as \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), where \(p\le2^m\).  One exact algorithm enumerates the \(2^p\) subsets and tests their unions.  A second uses branch masks: set \(D_0(\varnothing)=0\), \(D_0(U)=+\infty\) for nonempty \(U\subseteq\Omega\), and
\[
 D_i(U)=\min\{D_{i-1}(U),
 D_{i-1}(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i))+w(S_i)\}.
\tag{6}
\]
Induction on \(i\) proves that \(D_i(U)\) is the minimum cost of a subset of the first \(i\) protocols covering \(U\): an optimum either omits \(S_i\), giving the first term, or includes it, leaving \(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i)\), giving the second.  Thus \(D_p(\Omega)\) equals (3).  The two alternatives use respectively \(2^{O(p)}\) and \(2^{O(M)}p\) work after incidence construction.  Since \(p\le2^m\), choosing the smaller gives
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}).
\tag{7}
\]
Exact rational addition and comparison have polynomial bit cost because all action costs are binary rational.

The lexicographically first optimum is obtained by standard finite self-reduction, which we spell out.  Given a prefix of the canonical singleton-record encoding, force every completed record named by the prefix, reject intersecting ownership, subtract already owned branches, and charge every already used protocol once.  Recompute (6), or the protocol-subset alternative, on the remaining allowed witnesses and protocols.  The prefix has an optimum-cost completion exactly when this constrained optimum plus the forced cost equals (3).  Try the next bit values in lexicographic order and retain the first with an optimum completion.  The invariant that the retained prefix has such a completion holds initially by attainment and is preserved by the test.  At termination the certificate is optimal; an earlier optimum would contradict the choice at its first differing bit.  There are only \(M\) nonempty singleton records.  If
\[
 q_M=\left\lceil\log_2(M+1)\right\rceil,
\tag{8}
\]
the owner of each record is stored by its index in \(q_M\) bits, with index zero reserved for an empty marker.  Hence ownership uses \(Mq_M\) bits rather than \(M^2\).  The number of self-reduction calls is at most \(2^{O(L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) by (4) and the transcript-size lemma, so this factor is absorbed by (7).

Finally consider weighted greedy.  Starting with uncovered set \(R\), choose a protocol with nonempty gain \(g_S=|K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\cap R|\) minimizing \(w(S)/g_S\), and remove its newly covered branches.  Let \(W^*\) be (3).  If \(W^*=0\), some zero-cost cover exists and greedy always has a zero-ratio choice until completion, so its cost is zero.  Suppose \(W^*>0\).  For an optimum cover \(\mathcal P^*\),
\[
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P^*}|K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\cap R|\ge |R|,
 \qquad
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P^*}w(S)=W^*.
\tag{9}
\]
If every positive-gain member had ratio greater than \(W^*/|R|\), multiplying by its gain and summing would contradict (9).  Therefore greedy's ratio is at most \(W^*/|R|\).  Charge each newly covered branch that ratio.  Ordering branches by their cover time, the \(i\)-th covered branch is charged at most \(W^*/(M-i+1)\).  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{greedy}})
 \le W^*\sum_{r=1}^M\frac1r
 =H_M\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}.
\tag{10}
\]
This is the explicit harmonic refinement, on the present protocol-to-branch cover, of the published weighted-greedy logarithmic guarantee.  Scanning all \(p\le2^m\) sets in at most \(M\) rounds is absorbed by the incidence-construction time in (5).  This is a protocol-cover guarantee; it does not assert an approximation for selecting individual actions under arbitrary protocol synergy.
body.justification: The switching normal form induces an explicit weighted set cover on legal protocols and concrete branches.
body.gap: Exhaustive certificate-string search ignores both the branch-mask dynamic program and the protocol-subset alternative.
body.consumer: The planner obtains an exact optimizer, an uncovered-branch infeasibility witness, or an \(H_M\)-approximate protocol collection.
